subject.title: Provider key pools + bucket-aware cooldown/backoff on 429 (Gemini projects) to prevent retry storms

question: Should Gemini project bucket-aware key routing be a native provider/auth feature, a requirement folded into the broader provider-profile routing design, or an external sidecar/plugin pattern for now?
rationale: Current source has flat key rotation and profile cooldowns but no quota-bucket identity contract, so implementation requires maintainer intent on config shape, cooldown scope, and core-vs-plugin ownership.

options.title: Fold Into Provider-Pool Routing
options.body: Track this issue as the bucket-aware requirement for the broader provider-profile pool routing work so key pools, auth profiles, and quota groups share one design.

options.title: Add Narrow Native Bucket Metadata
options.body: Add a focused Gemini/API-key quota-bucket field and cooldown path, accepting a new compatibility-sensitive provider/auth config surface.

options.title: Keep It External For Now
options.body: Document the sidecar/plugin approach until maintainers confirm a missing core extension API or native provider-routing requirement.

recommendation.title: Fold Into Provider-Pool Routing
recommendation.body: Track this issue as the bucket-aware requirement for the broader provider-profile pool routing work so key pools, auth profiles, and quota groups share one design.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent fallback/auth-runtime ownership history makes this the best available routing owner for the provider/auth product decision.
